scenes.text: Every fall, people with Medicare are asked to pick from about thirty-two plans. Sixty-nine percent don't compare at all. Medicare Helper is a neutral Medicare counselor in your family's pocket. Here's how it works, in four steps.

scenes.title: Step 1 · Tell it
scenes.text: Step one: tell it who you're helping. Ana is helping her mom, Rosa. She just takes a photo of the pill bottle. It reads the label and works out how many Rosa takes a month.

scenes.title: Step 2 · See the real cost
scenes.text: Step two: see the real cost. Ana adds where Rosa lives and her other medicine. It checks every plan in Miami-Dade against her exact prescriptions: the cost in a typical year, the most she could pay in a bad year, and which drug needs the plan's approval first. Every number comes from Medicare's own plan files, and in four hundred forty test cases it landed within ten percent or a hundred dollars of Medicare's Plan Finder ninety-eight percent of the time.

scenes.title: Step 3 · Ask what families ask
scenes.text: Step three: the questions families actually ask. Is her doctor in network? It searches each plan's directory, says plainly when it found nothing, and tells you to call and confirm. Then one tap writes a short summary for the family, in Spanish, with every number checked by code against the comparison.

scenes.title: Step 4 · When care is cut
scenes.text: Step four: when care is cut. The nursing home says Medicare will stop paying. Rosa uses big-text mode, in Spanish, and takes a photo of the notice. It finds the appeal deadline, the number to call, and what to say. NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius reads the notice, and every date is computed and checked by code before it's shown.
Neutral. In English or Spanish. Her details stay on her phone. Medicare Helper.

end_card: Rosa is fictional. The plan data is real.
